drills.q: Name the three families under the 'quantum ML' label and rank by evidence.
drills.a: 1) Quantum simulation (VQE): credible physics, gated on hardware. 2) QAOA optimisation: unproven, loses empirically to classical heuristics so far. 3) QML on classical data: weakest; no scaled advantage through 2026.

drills.q: Why is VQE's energy always an upper bound on the ground state?
drills.a: Rayleigh-Ritz: <psi|H|psi> >= E_min for any normalised psi, with equality iff psi is the ground state. Any ansatz state yields a valid upper bound; optimisation tightens it from above.

drills.q: Your VQE hardware energies sit consistently ABOVE simulator optimum. Explain and fix.
drills.a: Depolarising noise biases expectation values upward (mixed states raise <H> toward maximally-mixed average). Fixes: error mitigation (ZNE), shorter-depth ansatz, fake-backend pre-checks; cannot fully remove without correction.

drills.q: A vendor cites a quantum kernel paper beating SVMs. Give the three audit questions.
drills.a: Was the classical baseline tuned or defaults? Is data-encoding circuit depth counted end-to-end? Does the gap survive standard benchmarks at scale rather than curated splits? Published scaled advantages do not exist as of 2026.

drills.q: Why might barren plateaus spare chemistry-inspired ansaetze but kill random ones?
drills.a: UCCSD-style circuits stay near low-excitation manifolds with symmetry constraints, keeping gradient signal localised; random hardware-efficient circuits explore uniformly over Hilbert space where almost all directions are indistinguishable - variance collapses as O(1/2^n).

drills.q: QAOA approximation ratio degrades past p=5 on hardware but not in simulation. Diagnose.
drills.a: Hardware noise compounding with depth: each added layer adds two-qubit gates whose ~1e-3 errors outweigh marginal structure discovery. Verify via noiseless sim at same depths; mitigate with error mitigation/layout work or accept depth ceiling.

drills.q: Explain why data loading kills most QML speedup claims in one paragraph.
drills.a: Encoding N-dimensional classical data into amplitudes needs log2(N) qubits but ~N-depth state preparation without QRAM; angle encoding scales linearly with features but caps expressivity. Either way the loading step consumes the claimed advantage unless the data is natively quantum.

drills.q: What would constitute legitimate evidence of QML advantage that does not exist today?
drills.a: Peer-reviewed result beating TUNED classical baselines on a natural dataset, with encoding costs included in runtime, scaling demonstrated beyond toy widths, and access assumptions stated. Nothing published meets all four through mid-2026.

drills.q: Why is SPSA preferred over Adam for variational loops on noisy hardware?
drills.a: SPSA estimates gradients from just 2 total evaluations per step regardless of parameter count (simultaneous random perturbations); per-parameter methods need 2P evaluations whose shot noise dominates at P in the hundreds. SPSA averages noise efficiently across steps.

drills.q: Draft the two-line executive answer: should we fund quantum ML now?
drills.a: Fund quantum simulation research pilots only if we own hard chemistry/materials problems; treat optimisation/QML-on-data as watch-list items because no quantum model beats strong classical baselines today and credible wins are gated on post-2028 error-corrected hardware.

drills.q: Your team is deciding whether to invest engineering time in a QML pilot for a real business problem in 2026. What's your recommendation?
drills.a: Recommend against committing significant resources to running the task on quantum hardware today â€” no reproducible advantage exists at relevant scale, and barren plateaus plus shot-count scaling make near-term scaling unlikely. Better use of limited investment: a small team monitoring the literature for claims surviving dequantization scrutiny, while primary effort stays on the best classical methods.

drills.q: If VQE always gives an upper bound on ground energy, does that mean more optimization steps always monotonically improve the estimate?
drills.a: Not necessarily â€” the guarantee is about the theoretical minimum over the ansatz family, not the optimizer's trajectory. A non-convex landscape, especially with barren plateaus, can cause stalling or getting stuck in a local minimum well above the true ground energy despite more steps being run.
